title: Valens Semiconductor Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Results
summary: Learn more about Valens' latest news from our marketing newsroom for industry experts, professionals and investors. Valens Semiconductor Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Results %
body_markdown:
- Delivered Q3 2026 revenue of $21.9 million, exceeding the top end of our guidance
- Q3 2026 gross margin: 62.2% GAAP; 64.4% non-GAAP
- Cash, cash equivalents and short-term deposits as of September 30, 2026: $74.7 million


HOD HASHARON, Israel, November 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Valens Semiconductor Ltd. (NYSE: VLN), a leading provider of high-performance connectivity chipsets, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.


“We are pleased with our performance in the third quarter, where we exceeded our guidance and delivered revenue of $21.9 million,” said Yoram Salinger, CEO of Valens Semiconductor. “One year into my tenure as CEO, I’m proud to introduce a new growth plan that builds on our strength in premium solutions while opening the door to significantly larger, mainstream markets. In audio-video, we announced the launch of the VS6310 chip, which will be the cornerstone for our strategy of embedding our technology inside a range of video conferencing devices. In automotive, we announced a strategic collaboration with leading image sensor manufacturer onsemi to bring A-PHY into high-volume automotive camera applications. We’re optimistic that our growth strategy will allow us to expand our share in the markets we serve”.


**Q3 2026 Business Highlights:**


- Announced the VS6310, a low-power USB3 extension chipset designed for integration directly into e/PTZ cameras, touch controllers, active cables and other small conference room peripherals.
- Partnered with onsemi on a cost-optimized integrated sensor for high-volume 3-megapixel automotive camera applications.
- New product launches based on the VS3000 and VS6320 chipsets by Sound Control Technologies, Blustream, Atlona, and Jabra.


**Q3 2026 Financial Highlights:**


- Q3 2026 revenue reached $21.9 million, exceeding our quarterly guidance of $21.3-$21.7 million, compared to $18.1 million in Q2 2026 and $17.3 million in Q3 2025.


- Q3 2026 Cross-Industry Business (“CIB”) revenue accounted for approximately 65% of total revenue at $14.0 million compared to $13.1 million in Q2 2026 and compared to $13.2 million in Q3 2025.


- Q3 2026 Automotive revenue accounted for approximately 35% of total revenue at $7.9 million, compared to $5.0 million in Q2 2026 and $4.1 million in Q3 2025, in line with our expectation and plan.


- Q3 2026 GAAP gross margin was 62.2% (non-GAAP gross margin was 64.4%), above our guidance. This is compared to a GAAP gross margin of 61.5% for Q2 2026 and 63.0% for Q3 2025 (non-GAAP gross margin of 64.3% in Q2 2026 and 66.7% in Q3 2025). On a segment basis, Q3 gross margin from CIB was 66.8% and gross margin from Automotive was 53.9%. This compares to a Q2 2026 gross margin of 69.2% and 41.5%, respectively, and a Q3 2025 gross margin of 69.1% and 43.2%, respectively. The decrease in Q3 CIB gross margin compared to Q2 2026 and Q3 2025 was mainly due to a change in product mix. The increase in Q3 automotive gross margin compared to Q2 2026 was due to lower testing facility expenses incurred to prioritize and support production requirements, as well as a change in product mix.
- Q3 2026 GAAP net loss amounted to $(5.5) million, compared to a net loss of $(8.1) million in Q2 2026 and a net loss of $(7.3) million in Q3 2025.
- Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $(2.7) million, better than the guidance range of a $(3.4)-$(2.8) million adjusted EBITDA loss. This compares to an adjusted EBITDA loss of $(4.2) million in Q2 2026 and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $(4.3) million in Q3 2025. The adjusted EBITDA improvement is related mainly to revenue increase, partially offset by planned tape out costs.
- Cash, cash equivalents and short-term deposits as of September 30, 2026, were $74.7 million. This compares to cash, cash equivalents and short-term deposits of $83.4 million as of June 30, 2026 and to cash, cash equivalents and short-term deposits of $92.6 million as of December 31, 2025. The decrease in cash was primarily reflects timing differences in collections, driven by the higher volume of revenues recognized toward the end of the third quarter and are expected to be collected in the following quarter, in line with standard payment terms.


**Financial Outlook for 2026**


Valens Semiconductor is reaffirming its previously announced guidance for the full year 2026 to be between $78 million to $81 million, toward the upper end of the range. Full year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA is expected to be in the range of $(14.9) million and $(12.9) million loss.


*Disclaimer: Valens Semiconductor does not provide GAAP net profit (loss) guidance as certain elements of net profit (loss), including share-based compensation expenses and warrant valuations, are not predictable due to the high variability and difficulty of making accurate forecasts. Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP measure. See the tables below for additional information regarding this and other non-GAAP metrics used in this release.*

**About Valens Semiconductor**


Valens Semiconductor (NYSE: VLN) is a leading provider of high-performance connectivity chipsets, enabling reliable, high-bandwidth, long-reach video transmission across the world’s most demanding applications. Valens’ chipsets are integrated into countless devices from leading customers, powering state-of-the-art audio-video installations, next-generation videoconferencing, Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving. Valens is a pioneer in connectivity technologies and a key contributor to leading industry standards, including HDBaseT® and MIPI A-PHY. For more information, visit[www.valens.com](http://www.valens.com/)

Adjusted EBITDA is defined as Net profit (loss) before financial income, net, income taxes, equity in earnings of investee and depreciation and amortization, further adjusted to exclude share-based compensation and change in fair value of earnout liability and Forfeiture Shares, which may vary from period-to-period, as well as certain batch production incident income. We caution investors that amounts presented in accordance with our definition of Adjusted EBITDA may not be comparable to similar measures disclosed by other issuers, because not all issuers calculate Adjusted EBITDA in the same manner. Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered as an alternative to Net loss or any other performance measures derived in accordance with GAAP or as an alternative to cash flows from operating activities as a measure of our liquidity.


Although we provide guidance for Adjusted EBITDA, we are not able to provide guidance for projected Net profit (loss), the most directly comparable GAAP measures. Certain elements of Net profit (loss), including share-based compensation expenses and warrant valuations, are not predictable due to the high variability and difficulty of making accurate forecasts. As a result, it is impractical for us to provide guidance on Net profit (loss) or to reconcile our Adjusted EBITDA guidance without unreasonable efforts. Consequently, no disclosure of projected Net profit (loss) is included. For the same reasons, we are unable to address the probable significance of the unavailable information.
